title: Module and abelian cohomology over an object of a ringed site agree
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of rings on $\mathcal C$, and $M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $M_{ab}$ for the underlying abelian sheaf. Work in a common universe containing the objects, arrows, ring and module values, and covering index sets, and assume the module category has enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every integer $q\geq0$, there is a canonical additive isomorphism $$R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,-)(M)\cong H^q(U,M_{ab}),$$ where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\operatorname{Ab}$ sends $P$ to $P(U)$, its right derived functors are computed by injective module resolutions, and $H^q(U,-)$ is the right derived functor of evaluation in abelian sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. These isomorphisms are natural in $M$ and are the identity of $M(U)$ in degree zero. No flatness of $\mathcal O$ over the constant integer sheaf and no injectivity of $M_{ab}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 03FD, label lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree, second displayed equality (cohomology over any object)

proof.text: Let T be forgetting module structure and F be evaluation of abelian sheaves at U. Exactness of T is clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful. Apply the already stated general-site theorem lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski (whose Lean statement is for any ringed site, despite the historical node name). It proves H^q(U,T(I))=0 for every injective module sheaf I and q>0, by the same 03FC/03F9 argument as the original plan. The natural Ext-cohomology/derived-evaluation comparison lem-sc-site-cohomology-right-derived-sections turns this into F.rightAcyclic(T(I)). All universes are u; enough injectives and HasExt for abelian sheaves come from the small-site Grothendieck-abelian instance.

source.place: Tag 03FD, second displayed equality and injective acyclicity paragraph; acyclic-resolution comparison uses Derived Categories Tags 015E and 015M

proof.text: For each M, choose its standard injective module resolution I. Exact T sends its augmentation to a quasi-isomorphism T(M)[0] -> T(I), whose terms are F-acyclic by the preceding step. Compose I.isoRightDerivedObj(T composed with F) with the inverse acyclic-resolution comparison F.rightDerivedObjIsoOfResolution. Both section complexes are the same complex. For a map f:M -> N, use InjectiveResolution.desc to lift f. Naturality of the mapped single-complex augmentation gives the required square; combine InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality with lem-sc-acyclic-comparison-natural. NatIso.ofComponents then assembles these explicit component isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03FD, second displayed equality and injective acyclicity paragraph; acyclic-resolution comparison uses Derived Categories Tags 015E and 015M

proof.text: Apply lem-sc-ext-derived-composite to T and F. Its isomorphism is characterized by every augmentation-compatible resolution lift. Evaluating its characterization on the standard resolutions and the standard descOfQuasiIso lift identifies it with the explicit component just constructed, by unfolding the acyclic-resolution comparison. The complex-composition isomorphism is the identity for T composed with F. Consequently the constructed natural isomorphism has the stated formula for every I,K,phi; cancel the terminal injective-resolution isomorphism to obtain the equation in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03FD, second displayed equality and injective acyclicity paragraph; acyclic-resolution comparison uses Derived Categories Tags 015E and 015M

proof.text: For q=0 choose a standard lift phi:T(I) -> K. After composing with iCycles, the two maps from F(T(M)) to cycles agree by the augmentation equation F(T(I.ι^0)) composed with F(phi^0)=F(K.ι^0); cancel the monomorphism iCycles. Naturality of homologyπ therefore identifies their maps to H^0. Substitute Mathlib InjectiveResolution.toRightDerivedZero_eq on both sides, use the resolution-lift formula from the preceding step, and cancel the injective-resolution comparison isomorphisms. This proves the asserted equality of the two degree-zero augmentations. No injectivity after forgetting or coefficient flatness is used.
